# bunnynet_loadbalancer_origin (Resource)

This resource manages a Load Balancer origin in bunny.net.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bunnynet_loadbalancer_origin" "DK" {
  loadbalancer = bunnynet_loadbalancer.test.id
  group        = bunnynet_loadbalancer_group.EU.id
  group_weight = 1
  name         = "DK"
  type         = "OriginUrl"
  url          = "https://origin-dk.example.net"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group` (Number) The ID of the Load Balancer group.
- `loadbalancer` (Number) The ID of the Load Balancer.
- `name` (String) The name of the Load Balancer origin.
- `type` (String) Options: `ComputeContainer`, `ComputeScript`, `OriginUrl`, `StorageZone`

### Optional

- `container_app_id` (String) The ID if the compute container app.
- `container_endpoint_id` (String) The ID if the compute container app endpoint.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Indicates whether the Load Balancer origin is enabled.
- `group_weight` (Number) The weight of the Load Balancer origin. Used in Load Balancers groups with method = "Weight"
- `host_header` (String) The host header that will be sent to the origin.
- `script` (Number) The ID of the linked compute script.
- `storagezone` (Number) The ID of the linked storage zone.
- `url` (String) The origin URL from where the files are fetched.
- `verify_ssl` (Boolean) Indicates whether the Origin's TLS certificate should be verified.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The unique ID of the Load Balancer origin.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import bunnynet_loadbalancer_group.test '123|EU|DK'
```
